---
title: "6 · Model assumptions and limitations"
description: "What your model quietly assumes about the ocean, and what happens when the ocean disagrees."
categories: [assumptions, spatial-temporal, class-imbalance]
---

Machine-learning methods are often described as assumption-free. They are not. They
make fewer assumptions about the *shape* of relationships than a linear model does,
which is a real advantage. But they make strong assumptions about how the data were
collected, and marine data violates most of them.

Two stations ten metres apart are not independent observations. A time series sampled
monthly for three years tells you little about a decadal cycle. Survey effort follows
ports, weather windows and funding. Predicting into unsampled depth or an unprecedented
temperature is extrapolation, whatever the model's confidence output says.

This is the section that determines whether the rest of the course helps you or
misleads you.

## In this section

- Independence of observations
- Linearity and nonlinearity
- Distributional assumptions
- Spatial and temporal dependence
- Uneven sampling and extrapolation
- Class imbalance
- When standard validation methods are inappropriate
- The limits of predicting outside the observed data range

::: {.callout-important}
If observations are spatially or temporally dependent, ordinary cross-validation will
overstate performance — sometimes dramatically. The fix is in
[7 · Validation](../07-validation/index.qmd).
:::
